CVE-2026-102894.title: GPUStack: SAML callback trusts an unverified SAMLResponse, allowing authentication bypass and account takeover
CVE-2026-102894.description: GPUStack is an open-source GPU cluster manager for AI model serving and GPU instance provisioning. CVE-2026-113782.title: ESP-IDF: Stack-Based Out-of-Bounds Write in Thread Border Router ND6 Option Parsing
CVE-2026-113782.description: ESP-IDF is the Espressif Internet of Things (IOT) Development Framework. From 5.2.0 until 5.2.8, 5.3.6, 5.4.5, 5.5.5, and 6.0.3, the OpenThread Border Router Neighbor Discovery packet handler trusts an attacker-controlled ICMPv6 option length while copying into a fixed stack buffer. A host on the same infrastructure link as the Border Router can send a crafted ICMPv6 Router Advertisement to its infrastructure interface whose oversized length causes an out-of-bounds write into adjacent stack memory. Firmware is affected only when CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_BORDER_ROUTER=y; Thread end devices, routers, and RCP firmware without the Border Router feature are unaffected. Exploitation requires no authentication or user interaction and can crash or reboot the device or corrupt adjacent stack state. CVE-2026-98931.title: mtd: spinand: fix NULL pointer dereference with no ECC engine
CVE-2026-98931.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mtd: spinand: fix NULL pointer dereference with no ECC engine

When "nand-no-ecc-engine" is set in DT, nanddev_get_ecc_engine() takes
the NAND_ECC_ENGINE_TYPE_NONE path and returns success while leaving
nand->ecc.engine NULL. The SPI-NAND code nevertheless dereferences it
unconditionally to test for a pipelined engine, so probing such a
device oopses immediately.

Rather than open-coding the test three times, add a
nand_ecc_is_pipelined() helper to the NAND core that folds the NULL
check into the integration comparison, and use it everywhere. Future
callers then cannot reintroduce the problem.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

regulator: tps6594-regulator: Fix n_linear_ranges for TPS65224 BUCK2-4

The TPS65224 BUCK2, BUCK3 and BUCK4 descriptors pass 4 as
n_linear_ranges, but tps65224_bucks_2_3_4_ranges[] only has two
entries, covering selectors 0x00-0x45.

lookup of a selector above 0x45 reads past the end of the array and

normal registration path when the core checks the voltage constraints
against every selector. TPS652G1 uses the same descriptors and is
affected too.

Use ARRAY_SIZE() so the count always matches the table.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

rust: configfs: fix data offset calculation for subsystem callbacks

`get_group_data()` chooses between `Group::<Parent>::container_of()` and
`Subsystem::<Parent>::container_of()` based on whether `this` represents
the root group of a configfs subsystem. It detects this by checking
`(*this).cg_subsys.is_null()`, but `link_group()` in `fs/configfs/dir.c`
unconditionally sets `cg_subsys` for every `config_group` attached anywhere
in a registered subsystem, including the subsystem's own `su_group`. The
only `config_group` with a NULL `cg_subsys` is the configfs root, on which
userspace cannot trigger callbacks. The check is therefore always false at
runtime, and the `Subsystem` branch is dead. Subsystem-level callbacks
reach the `Group` branch and may read `data` at the wrong offset.
